Recognize monetary units.
Distinguish saving from spending.

subtopics.title: Distinguish goods from services

Explain how goods and services are obtained.

subtopics.title: Differentiate needs from wants

topics.title: Civil Rights

subtopics.title: Explore the similarities and differences of individuals and families

Identify examples of similarities and differences.
Explain the importance of both similarities and differences to individuals, families, and communities.

Identify types of diversity in the classroom (e.g., cultural, ethnic, students with disabilities, etc.).

topics.title: Geography

outcomes.text: Differentiate landforms from bodies of water.

subtopics.title: Recognize representations of the Earth

outcomes.text: Discuss various representations of the Earth.
Explain that maps and globes help identify location and physical features of the Earth.
Compare and contrast maps and globes.

topics.title: History

subtopics.title: Recognize symbols, customs, and celebrations of local communities, Mississippi, and the United States

State the Pledge of Allegiance and patriotic songs as expressions of patriotism.

topics.title: Civics

subtopics.title: Differentiate the rights and responsibilities citizens have in varying roles

Discuss how citizens show patriotism and respect for their communities and country.

Describe what it means to be employed.

subtopics.title: Determine how people meet their basic needs

outcomes.text: Identify basic needs.
Explain how basic needs are met.
Classify items or services as needs and wants.
Examine how people prioritize spending and saving to meet their needs.

topics.title: Civil Rights

subtopics.title: Evaluate the role of cooperation and compromise within and across various groups

outcomes.text: Define cooperation and compromise.
Identify examples of cooperation and compromise at home and school.
Analyze how cooperation and compromise supports problem solving in and among different cultures, customs, and traditions.

subtopics.title: Examine the diverse cultures found at school and in the local community

outcomes.text: Define culture.
Identify various cultures at school and in the local community.
Recognize ways people celebrate their diverse cultural heritage.
Compare and contrast ways people celebrate their diverse cultural heritage.

topics.title: Geography

subtopics.title: Demonstrate a global sense of place

outcomes.text: Identify the seven continents and five major oceans.
Classify the major landforms, and bodies of water on a map (e.g., mountains, hills, lakes, oceans, rivers, etc.).
Describe places in relation to one another using cardinal and intermediate directions.

subtopics.title: Examine the relationship between location, climate, physical features, and how people live

outcomes.text: Recognize characteristics of the local region.

Describe how location impacts daily life for residents in various communities (e.g., shelter, clothing, food, activities, etc.).

subtopics.title: Interpret maps using directions

outcomes.text: Demonstrate map skills through vocabulary.
Identify and define cardinal and intermediate directions, compass rose, map symbol and map key.
Construct maps using cardinal and intermediate directions, a compass rose, map symbols, and a map key.

topics.title: History

subtopics.title: Analyze the influence of significant historical figures and events from the history of the United States

outcomes.text: Identify historical figures who are used as symbols in United States culture.
Examine the significant contributions of historical figures to the local community, state, and United States.
Examine how the United States commemorates historical events through the celebration of national holidays.

subtopics.title: Analyze various aspects of historic and modern life in the United States

outcomes.text: Compare and contrast historic and modern forms of communication and sharing of information.
Identify forms of technology and illustrate changes in how it was made and used from its conception to the present (e.g., telephone, assistive technology devices, etc.).
Evaluate how apparel has changed through history, including how and why items are chosen and purchased.
Compare and contrast Americans' use of free time in the past and present.

topics.title: Civics

subtopics.title: Differentiate civic virtues from civic responsibilities, then evaluate their role in communities

outcomes.text: Identify civic virtues and civic responsibilities.
Discuss how common civic virtues among citizens help create peaceful and orderly communities.
Compare civic responsibilities to responsibilities of home and school.

subtopics.title: Assess how rules and laws are created to provide equal and fair service and protection to all citizens

outcomes.text: Discuss importance of fair rules and laws applied to all citizens.
Analyze the fairness of rules and laws.
Identify who is responsible for creating and enforcing rules and laws.
Discuss how laws are fairly created and fairly enforced to protect all the citizens of a community (e.g., civil rights, laws to protect Americans with disabilities, etc.).

topics.title: Economics

subtopics.title: Evaluate how the availability of resources impacts the local economy

outcomes.text: Define economy and resource.
Categorize resources as natural, renewable, and non-renewable.
Explain people as a resource in the local community.
Examine the relationship between resources and jobs in the local community.

subtopics.title: Assess the relationship between consumers and producers in obtaining goods and services to meet needs

outcomes.text: Define consumers and producers.
Differentiate consumers from producers.
Examine the interdependence of consumers and producers.
Discuss the connection between resources and producers in the local community.
Define barter system and monetary system.
Compare and contrast the barter and monetary systems of trade to meet needs.

subtopics.title: Recognize factors that affect the price and availability of goods and services

outcomes.text: Define supply and demand.
Evaluate how the availability of resources impacts the price of goods and services.
Examine how budgets help individuals and families choose how to spend and save money.

subtopics.title: Identify the role of financial institutions within the community

outcomes.text: Identify various types of financial institutions and their role in the community.
Identify services provided by the various financial institutions in the community.

topics.title: Civil Rights

subtopics.title: Determine how traditions and customs create unity and celebrate diversity within and across various groups

outcomes.text: Recognize the cultural contributions of various groups within our community.
Examine how cultures, and their traditions and customs, have changed over time.
Evaluate the qualities that build unity among diverse populations.

subtopics.title: Evaluate how diverse cultures build unity in a community

outcomes.text: Define respect, tolerance, and acceptance.
Examine the relationship between respect, tolerance, and acceptance and building unity across cultures.
Recognize similarities from the various cultures of the local community.

topics.title: Geography

subtopics.title: Analyze various types of maps

outcomes.text: Categorize map types by representation and usage (e.g., topographic, physical, political, thematic, etc.).
Identify political and physical borders in the United States and across the globe.
Define urban, suburban, and rural.
Locate urban, suburban, and rural areas in Mississippi and United States.

subtopics.title: Examine the connection between physical features of the Earth and where people choose to live

outcomes.text: Define human settlements and population distribution.
Evaluate human settlements and population distribution around physical features of the Earth.
Determine reasons for human settlement near physical features of the Earth.

subtopics.title: Interpret maps using latitude and longitude

outcomes.text: Define latitude and longitude.
Locate the major lines of latitude and longitude of the Earth.
Identify then compare hemispheres of the Earth.

subtopics.title: Analyze human modifications to the Earth

outcomes.text: Identify human modifications to the Earth.
Compare and contrast the positive and negative impacts of human modifications on the Earth.

topics.title: History

subtopics.title: Evaluate how people and events have shaped the local community, state, and nation through primary sources

outcomes.text: Identify various primary sources (e.g., Primary – letters, diaries, autobiographies, speeches, interviews; Secondary – magazine articles, textbooks, encyclopedia entries, biographies, etc.).
Use various primary sources to investigate significant people and events of the past.
Examine historical events from multiple perspectives by utilizing primary sources.

subtopics.title: Examine the relationship between history and time

outcomes.text: Identify vocabulary to express periods of time.
Illustrate events chronologically on a timeline.
Compare and contrast the eras of United States history.

topics.title: Civics

subtopics.title: Examine the influence of democratic values on the lives of citizens

outcomes.text: Define democracy.
Recognize fundamental democratic values.
Discuss the evidence of democratic values at home, school, and local organizations.

subtopics.title: Demonstrate knowledge of the three branches of government at the federal, state, and local levels

outcomes.text: Identify the three branches of government and the purpose of each branch.
Discuss the roles of leaders in each branch of government at the federal, state, and local levels, including both municipal and county governments.
Recognize locations where government is practiced at the national, state, and local levels.
Compare and contrast services provided to communities and citizens by the federal, state, and local governments (e.g., security, people with disabilities, human services, etc.).

subtopics.title: Examine the requirements of civic leadership

outcomes.text: Identify the qualifications for candidacy at the federal, state, and local levels.
Analyze the common character traits and civic virtues of national, state, and local leaders.
Contrast the responsibilities of elected leaders and citizens in maintaining peaceful and orderly communities.

topics.title: Economics

subtopics.title: Investigate how local governments obtain and use money to benefit their communities

outcomes.text: Define tax.
Discuss the types and purpose of taxes paid by citizens to the government (e.g., sales tax, property tax, income tax, etc.).
Identify goods and services provided by a local government to its community.
Examine how a local community benefits from the goods and services provided by the local government.

subtopics.title: Evaluate how individuals and communities use resources and trade to meet needs

outcomes.text: Define trade, import, and export.
Contrast imports and exports.
Identify local resources and products exported from the local community and state.
Trace the origin of products for sale in the local community.
Compare and contrast producing and buying goods to meet needs.

subtopics.title: Analyze the factors of population distribution

outcomes.text: Define economic development.
Examine the relationship between economic development, employment opportunities, and where people choose to live.
Evaluate the impact of an individual's knowledge and skills on their opportunities for employment and income.
Explain how the availability of resources influences where people live.

topics.title: Civil Rights

subtopics.title: Examine the Declaration of Independence and the Bill of Rights to recognize the principles of democracy and identify civil liberties

outcomes.text: Identify principals of democracy within the Declaration of Independence.
Define and identify civil liberties within the First Amendment.
Compare and contrast principles of democracy and civil liberties.
Explain how individuals exercise principles of democracy and civil liberties in daily life.

subtopics.title: Assess the reliance of democracy on citizen participation

outcomes.text: Define voting, suffrage, and franchise.
Explain the voting process.
Illustrate the expansion of voting rights in America.
Identify how citizens participate in democracy apart from exercising the right to vote.

topics.title: Geography

subtopics.title: Analyze how humans have altered the Earth to meet their needs

outcomes.text: Define residential, commercial, industrial, and agricultural.
Describe the residential, commercial, industrial, and agricultural areas of the local community and state.
Explain how humans have altered the physical environment for shelter, work, and recreation.
Discuss how human modifications have affected the environment.

subtopics.title: Investigate natural disasters' effect on the Earth

outcomes.text: Define natural disaster.
Identify characteristics of a natural disaster.
Explain how local, state, and national governments cooperate to manage natural disasters.
Evaluate settlement patterns after a natural disaster.

subtopics.title: Assess energy sources of the Earth

outcomes.text: Define renewable and nonrenewable resources.
Identify sources of energy (e.g., oil, petroleum, nuclear power, solar power, etc.).
Categorize energy sources as renewable and nonrenewable.
Examine the impact that human use of resources has on the Earth.

subtopics.title: Interpret and recognize maps, graphs, and other representations of the Earth

outcomes.text: Analyze patterns of population distributions.

topics.title: History

subtopics.title: Analyze the different types of government throughout history, such as dictatorship, monarchy, aristocracy, representative democracy, and direct democracy

outcomes.text: Define dictatorship, monarchy, aristocracy, representative democracy, and direct democracy.
Cite an example of each type of government from history.
Compare and contrast the different types of government related to source of authority, how leaders are chosen, limits on power, and the role of citizens.

subtopics.title: Examine the framework of the United States government

outcomes.text: Discuss why the United States was established as a representative democracy.
Evaluate the importance of checks and balances to a representative democracy.

topics.title: Mississippi Studies and Regions

subtopics.title: Describe the physical geography and natural resources of the ten regions of Mississippi

outcomes.text: Identify on a map the ten geographical regions of Mississippi (Yazoo Delta, Black Belt, Jackson Prairie, Gulf Coast, Loess Hills, North Central Hills, Flatwoods, Pontotoc Ridge, Tennessee River Hills, and Piney Woods).
Describe features of each region.
Compare and contrast the ten geographical regions of Mississippi in terms of soil, landforms, etc.
Compare and contrast major natural resources throughout Mississippi on a map (e.g., oil, agricultural, etc.).

subtopics.title: Examine the exploration and settlement of the Mississippi Territory

outcomes.text: Map and describe the settlements of the Mississippi Territory (e.g., Natchez, Washington, Port Gibson, Columbia, Winchester, Mobile, Huntsville, etc.).

Trace the routes of explorers (e.g., Hernando de Soto, Rene Robert Caveliersieur de La Salle, Pierre Le Moyne d 'Iberville, Jacques Marquette, Louis Jolliet, etc.) and discuss the impact on settlements in the Mississippi Territory.
Explain how differing beliefs regarding land ownership, religion, and culture led to conflicts between Europeans and Native Americans in the Mississippi Territory.

subtopics.title: Investigate the Native American tribes of historic Mississippi

outcomes.text: Identify the location of major tribes within Mississippi: Choctaw, Chickasaw, and Natchez.
Compare and contrast the cultures and lives of the Choctaw, Chickasaw, and Natchez tribes of historic Mississippi (e.g., homes, roles, beliefs, clothes, games, traditions, food, etc.).
Discuss the impact of the removal of Native Americans from Mississippi.

subtopics.title: Describe Mississippi's entry into statehood

outcomes.text: Trace Mississippi's progression from territory to statehood.
Define political and geographic reasons for changes in location of Mississippi's state capitol.

subtopics.title: Describe the Antebellum society of Mississippi

outcomes.text: Outline the rise of Mississippi cotton culture.
Link cotton culture to the rise of slavery.
Discuss the leaders of the abolition movement and the importance to the end of slavery in the South.

subtopics.title: Analyze Mississippi's role in the Civil War

outcomes.text: Identify the Mississippi leaders of the secession and the Civil War.
Outline the cause and effects of slavery that led Mississippi to secede from the Union in 1861 and subsequently enter the Civil War.
Investigate how Mississippi supported the Civil War through economic and military efforts.
Compare and contrast the societal roles on the homefront and battlefront during and after the Civil War.

subtopics.title: Evaluate the impact of Reconstruction and Post-Reconstruction on Mississippi

outcomes.text: Contrast life from the Antebellum period to post Civil War (e.g., population, economy, government, infrastructure, etc.).
Explain the use of sharecroppers as a response to the end of slavery.
Describe how the Jim Crow laws disenfranchised African Americans in Mississippi.

subtopics.title: Analyze the Civil Rights Movement to determine the social, political, and economic impact on Mississippi

outcomes.text: Define discrimination, prejudice, segregation, integration, suffrage, and civil rights.

Identify important figures of the modern Civil Rights Movement including Mississippians (e.g., Martin Luther King Jr., Rosa Parks, Medgar Evers, James Meredith, Fannie Lou Hamer, Charles Evers, etc.).

Identify and explain events of the modern Civil Rights Movement, including Brown v. Board of Education (1954), Jim Crow laws, Freedom Summer, and James Meredith's admission to the University of Mississippi.
Analyze the importance of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 as it relates to Mississippians.

subtopics.title: Explain how literature, the arts, architecture, and music distinguish Mississippi from other places

outcomes.text: Identify Mississippians known for their artwork, music, architecture, and literature (e.g., Wyatt Waters, William Herd, Walter Anderson, B.B. King, Elvis Presley, Marty Stewart, Eudora Welty, Willie Morris, etc.).
Describe how literature, the arts, architecture, and music affect tourism within the state.

subtopics.title: Describe the impact of significant historical figures and events in Mississippi's past and present

outcomes.text: Cite symbols and explain historical figures that are used in Mississippi's culture (e.g., monuments, place names, etc.).
Examine events that are significant to Mississippi culture.

subtopics.title: Evaluate how geographic and economic factors influence life and work in Mississippi

outcomes.text: Describe the division of labor within Mississippi (e.g., government, industry, agriculture, etc.).
Determine how land use impacts Mississippi's economy (e.g., cotton farming vs. soybean farming, pastureland vs. industrial development, beaches vs. casinos, landfills vs. parks, etc.).
Explain the benefits and challenges of trade for Mississippi.
Describe the economic impact of natural disasters (e.g., hurricanes, tornadoes, earthquakes, etc.).

Identify and locate the main mountain ranges, rivers, and other key bodies of water.

Determine how tribes in different regions used their environment to obtain, food, clothing, and shelter.
Differentiate the lives and cultures of Native American tribes by region or territory.

Explain the causes and effects of the Columbian Exchange.

subtopics.title: Examine the economic, political, and religious reasons for the founding of colonial settlements

Compare and contrast colonial life in the different regions (e.g., New England, Middle, Southern, etc.) including resources, way of life, economics, local government, etc.
Contrast the views of land use and ownership by Native Americans and colonists.

Discuss the contributions of African Americans, women, and ordinary citizens in general to the American Revolution.
Examine efforts to mobilize support for the American Revolution by the Minutemen, Committees of Correspondence, First Continental Congress, Sons of Liberty, and the Second Continental Congress.
Explain the colonial victory of the American Revolution.
Summarize the effects of the Treaty of Paris of 1783 on the development of the United States.

Analyze the shortcomings of the Articles of Confederation.
Explain how the Northwest Ordinance influenced the framers of the Constitution.
Identify significant attendees of the Constitutional Convention.

Explain historically significant people and events that shaped America (e.g., our first president, etc.).
